cell_type.evidence: LC-MS proteomic analysis using top-down and bottom-up combined strategies via Filter-Aided Sample Preparation (FASP) was applied to the secretome of mesenchymal stromal cells isolated from the amniotic membrane of human term placenta in the attempt to define the profile of its intact as well as digested proteome and of the biomolecules possibly involved in the immunomodulatory property exerted.

material_type.evidence: The proteome of the human amniotic mesenchymal stromal cells secretome was characterized by analyzing four different batches of secretome pool (Pools I-IV) by a modified Filter-Aided Sample Preparation (FASP, 10 kDa molecular mass filter cut-off) protocol, named C-FASP, able to prepare the sample in one step for top-down and bottom-up (using trypsin digestion) combined analysis applied to the filtrate (< 10 kDa) and to the retained (> 10 kDa) fractions, respectively.
